'''''Gladiolus communis''''', the '''eastern gladiolus''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''common corn-flag''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Gladiolus Communis |url=http://the.botanical-magazine.com/flower/gladiolus-communis |publisher=the.botanical-magazine.com |access-date=3 March 2018 |archive-date=3 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303110056/http://the.botanical-magazine.com/flower/gladiolus-communis |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="rhs">{{cite web |title=Gladiolus communis |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/99828/i-Gladiolus-communis-i/Details |publisher=rhs.org |access-date=3 March 2018}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Iridaceae, [[native plant|native]] to [[temperateness|temperate]] northern Africa, western Asia and southern Europe, from the [[Mediterranean]] to the [[Caucasus]],<ref name="rhs"/> and widely naturalised in frost-free locations elsewhere – such as coastal parts of the southwestern British Isles.<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/gladiolus-communis |title=Flora of the Isles of Scilly |year=1971 |publisher=David & Charles}}</ref>

It is a vigorous [[corm]]ous [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|1|m|0|abbr=on}} tall with linear leaves and bright pink flowers in spring. Two [[subspecies]] are identified:
*''G. communis'' subsp. ''communis''
*''[[Gladiolus × byzantinus|G. communis'' subsp. ''byzantinus]]'' ([[Philip Miller|Mill.]]) A. P. Ham.
In cultivation the latter has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Gladiolus communis'' subsp. ''byzantinus'' AGM |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/89297/Gladiolus-communis-subsp-byzantinus/Details |work=RHS Plant Finder |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=14 July 2020}}</ref><ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book |title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants |year=2008 |publisher=Dorling Kindersley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1405332965 |pages=1136}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=July 2017 |page=43 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=2 March 2018}}</ref>
